For the appellant
 Mr. Anand Keshari
 ...

For the State
 In re: Cran 1 of 2023
 1.

This application has been filed with a prayer for bail under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal
Procedure.
2.

Mr. Sudipto Maitra, learned Senior Counsel, on behalf of the appellant, at the outset, has submitted that on the scrutiny of the evidence it cannot be said that this is an offence under Sections 306/498A of the Indian Penal Code.
According to Mr. Maitra, this is a case of accident only as it appears from the evidence.
However, Mr. Maitra, learned Senior Counsel, on behalf of the appellant has submitted that the appellant/accused remained on bail during trial and it is a sentence of term imprisonment.
3. Mr. Anand Keshari, learned advocate, appearing on behalf of the State, raises formal objection.

4. Given facts and circumstances and considering the term imprisonment, I find it justified to allow the prayer for bail as there is no possibility of disposing of this appeal within short period of time.
5. Accordingly, the prayer for bail stands allowed.

6. The appellant/accused, namely, Santanu Roy shall furnish fresh bond of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Santanu Roy vs The State Of West Bengal on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141691525/
1 thirty thousand only), with two sureties of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees fifteen thousand only) each, subject to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sealdah, South 24-Parganas and on further condition that the appellant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court without prior permission of the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sealdah, South 24-Parganas.
